How unstable a stock's trading activity is from day to day (volume-of-volume), and how unstable its risk is (vol-of-vol), are overpriced, so the stable end should earn more. Chordia, Subrahmanyam & Anshuman (2001) found that a higher CV of turnover means lower returns. The proposed mechanism is attention shocks driving retail overpricing (Barber-Odean 2008), with Baltussen et al. (2018) for vol-of-vol.
